title: uPD1990A and uPD4990A command set
covers: the commands of the uPD1990A and uPD4990A, chosen by the C pins or the serial command register and latched by STB

rows.text: Register Hold is selected by C2 C1 C0 = 0 0 0, or by the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 0 0 0 0.
Register Hold makes the DATA OUT pin output a 1 Hz signal.
With the 3-bit command Register Hold holds the 40-bit shift register, and the year function is ineffective.
With the serial command Register Hold holds the 48-bit shift register but not the command register.
Register Shift is selected by C2 C1 C0 = 0 0 1, or by the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 0 0 0 1.
Register Shift outputs the least significant bit of the shift register on DATA OUT.
With the 3-bit command the 40-bit shift register data can be shifted, and the year function is ineffective.
With the serial command the 52-bit shift registers, command register included, can be shifted; the command register can always be shifted in serial command transfer mode.
In test mode Register Shift outputs 32 Hz on the TP pin.
In test mode Register Shift also has an 8192 Hz signal input to the time counter.
Time Set and Counter Hold is selected by C2 C1 C0 = 0 1 0, or by the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 0 0 1 0.
With the 3-bit command Time Set transfers the 40-bit shift register to the time counter, and the year function is ineffective.
With the serial command Time Set transfers the 48-bit shift register to the time counter.
Time Set outputs the least significant bit of the shift register on DATA OUT.
Time Set holds the time counter.
Time Set resets stages 10 to 15 of the 15 stage binary divider.
The 15 stage binary divider is reset and the time counter released by the commands [0,0,0], [0,0,1] and [0,1,1], or serially [0,0,0,0], [0,0,0,1] and [0,0,1,1].
The time setting accuracy is plus or minus 15.625 ms.
After Time Set the 40-/48-bit shift register is held and its data cannot be shifted.
Time Set also hands the time counter to the RTC interface with set_time, using the year byte even with the 3-bit command.
In test mode Time Set holds the TP pin at a low level.
Time Read is selected by C2 C1 C0 = 0 1 1, or by the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 0 0 1 1.
With the 3-bit command Time Read transfers the time counter to the 40-bit shift register, and the year function is ineffective.
With the serial command Time Read transfers the time counter to the 48-bit shift register.
Time Read makes the DATA OUT pin output a 1 Hz signal.
After Time Read the 40-/48-bit shift register is held and its data cannot be shifted.
At a 32768 Hz clock MAME gives the uPD4990A type a 1 Hz DATA OUT pulse here, but the uPD1990A type 0.5 Hz, or 512 Hz in test mode.
In the function-mode output table, Time Read outputs 32 Hz on the TP pin.
In the function-mode output table, Time Read also has an 8192 Hz signal input to the time counter.
TP = 64 Hz Set Mode is selected by C2 C1 C0 = 1 0 0, or by the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 0 1 0 0.
The command outputs a 64 Hz signal, at 50 % duty, on the TP pin.
With the 3-bit command the interval timer stops.
With the 3-bit command the year function is ineffective.
TP = 256 Hz Set Mode is selected by C2 C1 C0 = 1 0 1, or by the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 0 1 0 1.
The command outputs a 256 Hz signal, at 50 % duty, on the TP pin.
With the 3-bit command the interval timer stops.
With the 3-bit command the year function is ineffective.
TP = 2048 Hz Set Mode is selected by C2 C1 C0 = 1 1 0, or by the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 0 1 1 0.
The command outputs a 2048 Hz signal, at 50 % duty, on the TP pin.
With the 3-bit command the interval timer stops.
With the 3-bit command the year function is ineffective.
TP = 4098 Hz Set Mode, as the data sheet text names it, is allowed only for the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 0 1 1 1.
The serial command 0 1 1 1 outputs 4096 Hz on the TP pin, according to the command table.
The command text says a 4098 Hz signal, at 50 % duty, is output on the TP pin.
The command stops the interval timer.
MAME's divisor 8 gives a TP output of clock/8 Hz, 4096 Hz at a 32768 Hz clock, not the 4098 Hz of the text.
TP = 1 second Interval Set Mode (counter reset & start) is the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 1 0 0 0.
The command outputs a 1 second interval signal on the TP pin, with the interval counter reset and started.
TP = 10 second Interval Set Mode (counter reset & start) is the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 1 0 0 1.
The command outputs a 10 second interval signal on the TP pin, with the interval counter reset and started.
TP = 30 second Interval Set Mode (counter reset & start) is the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 1 0 1 0.
The command outputs a 30 second interval signal on the TP pin, with the interval counter reset and started.
TP = 60-second Interval Set Mode (counter reset & start) has the code [1, 0, 1, 1].
The command outputs a 60 second interval signal on the TP pin, with the interval counter reset and started.
Interval Output Flag Reset has the code [1, 1, 0, 0].
The command resets the interval signal output to the TP pin.
The interval timer counter continues the operation.
MAME's case for this command holds only a TODO comment and a break, and does nothing to reset an interval signal.
Interval Timer Clock Run has the code [1, 1, 0, 1].
The command resets the timer that outputs interval signals and then starts it.
MAME's case for this command holds only a TODO comment and a break, and does not reset or start any interval timer.
Interval Timer Clock Stop has the code [1, 1, 1, 0].
The command stops the timer that outputs interval signals.
The output status does not change.
MAME's case for this command holds only a TODO comment and a break, and does not stop any interval timer.
TEST MODE SET is the serial command C3' C2' C1' C0' = 1 1 1 1, given with C2 C1 C0 = 1 1 1.
The command sets the test mode.
C2 C1 C0 = 1 1 1 sets the serial command transfer mode.
When commands are input through C2, C1 and C0, the year function is ineffective.
Generally February has 28 days; the 29th can be set optionally, and the day after February 29 can be set to March 1 automatically.
In the 3-bit command mode the interval timer is in the halt state.
The test mode is cancelled by C2 C1 C0 = 0 0 0 to 1 1 0.
MAME also stops its time-counter timer and its DATA OUT pulse timer when it sets the test mode.
MAME clears its test-mode flag when the code is 0x00 or from 0x04 to 0x0E, so the 3-bit codes 0x01 to 0x03 do not clear it.
